scenes.tts: An osprey lifts a menhaden from the Chesapeake Bay. Where did the energy inside that fish begin? Follow one glowing packet backward through the moving water.
scenes.visual: Open inside one carried world: a side-view Chesapeake Bay filling at least sixty percent of the frame height. A PURPLE osprey rises at upper right with an ORANGE menhaden. GREEN phytoplankton drift near the sunlit surface, BLUE zooplankton pulse below, and GREY decomposers move along the bottom. GOLD sunlight shimmers and BLUE water ripples. Freeze one GOLD packet inside the caught fish, then extend a dotted question path backward. Show 'Where did this energy begin?' Colour map for this film, by organism, never by consumer order: energy and sunlight GOLD; phytoplankton GREEN; zooplankton BLUE; menhaden ORANGE; ospreys PURPLE; larger fish TEAL; decomposers GREY; heat RED. Never show a legend that names a consumer order for a colour.
scenes.narration: An osprey lifts a menhaden from the Chesapeake Bay. Where did the energy inside that fish begin? Follow one glowing packet backward through the moving water.

scenes.visual: Keep the Bay moving behind a dark translucent band. Show only 'Follow the Energy Arrows', then remove the band while the fish keep schooling.

scenes.tts: The Bay is an ecosystem, which includes living things and their nonliving surroundings. Light, water, and temperature are abiotic factors. Organisms, their parts, and their wastes are biotic factors. A change in either kind can reshape the community.
scenes.visual: Keep the Bay layout fixed. A bracket grows around the full scene and labels it 'ecosystem'. GOLD rays, moving BLUE water, and a large thermometer pulse under 'abiotic'. The osprey, fish, plankton, one feather, and one waste particle pulse under 'biotic'. Keep no more than six objects labelled.
scenes.narration: The Bay is an ecosystem, which includes living things and their nonliving surroundings. Light, water, and temperature are abiotic factors. Organisms, their parts, and their wastes are biotic factors. A change in either kind can reshape the community.

scenes.tts: The trail ends at sunlight reaching phytoplankton, tiny drifting algae. They are producers because they make food using light energy. That stored energy can enter the living food web. Most ecosystems need new energy entering again and again.
scenes.visual: Reverse the dotted trail until it reaches a GOLD sun ray. Enlarge one GREEN phytoplankton cartoon at centre. The ray enters a plain block inside it labelled 'stored food'; do not draw molecules. The block glows while nearby producers drift. Keep the rest of the Bay visible and moving.
scenes.narration: The trail ends at sunlight reaching phytoplankton, tiny drifting algae. They are producers because they make food using light energy. That stored energy can enter the living food web. Most ecosystems need new energy entering again and again.

scenes.tts: A zooplankton eats the producer. A menhaden eats that zooplankton. An osprey catches the menhaden. Each eater receives some stored energy from its food. The packet changes location, but it still follows the food.
scenes.visual: Arrange four large cartoons across the water: GREEN phytoplankton, BLUE zooplankton, ORANGE menhaden, and PURPLE osprey. Animate each eating action in order. The GOLD packet moves with the food and settles briefly inside each eater. Leave unlabeled gaps between the organisms for arrows.
scenes.narration: A zooplankton eats the producer. A menhaden eats that zooplankton. An osprey catches the menhaden. Each eater receives some stored energy from its food. The packet changes location, but it still follows the food.

scenes.tts: The arrows are missing. If each arrow shows energy movement, should it point toward the food or toward the eater? Choose before anything moves.
scenes.visual: Replace every gap with a double-headed dashed line. Show the large question 'Which way does energy move?' Keep the GOLD packet pulsing inside the producer. Water ripples and all organisms breathe or sway, but reveal no direction.
scenes.narration: The arrows are missing. If each arrow shows energy movement, should it point toward the food or toward the eater? Choose before anything moves.

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Hold both possible arrowheads and the question. The packet pulses, plankton drift, and water shimmers. Do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: Arrows point from food to eater, the same direction the energy packet moves. This straight route is one food chain. It is one path, not the whole ecosystem. Read every arrow by asking where the stored energy goes.
scenes.visual: Transform each double-headed line into one bold GOLD arrow pointing from food to eater. Run the packet along the complete route. Add the label 'one food chain' beneath it. On 'one path', narrow a bright outline around only this route while the dim Bay remains active behind it.
scenes.narration: Arrows point from food to eater, the same direction the energy packet moves. This straight route is one food chain. It is one path, not the whole ecosystem. Read every arrow by asking where the stored energy goes.

scenes.tts: Menhaden can also eat phytoplankton directly. Larger fish can eat menhaden too. New arrows join the first path. Linked food chains become a food web. That web reveals how a change can reach several organisms.
scenes.visual: Bend the chain back into the Bay. Add a direct GOLD arrow from GREEN phytoplankton to ORANGE menhaden. Add one TEAL larger fish and an arrow from menhaden to that fish. More GOLD packets take different branches. Transform the 'food chain' label into 'food web'.
scenes.narration: Menhaden can also eat phytoplankton directly. Larger fish can eat menhaden too. New arrows join the first path. Linked food chains become a food web. That web reveals how a change can reach several organisms.

scenes.tts: On the longer path, the osprey is a third-order consumer. On a shorter path, it is second-order. The animal stays the same. Its order depends on the chosen path. Consumer order describes a position on one route.
scenes.visual: Keep the PURPLE osprey fixed. Highlight the longer route and place three large step blocks beside it, numbered only on screen. Then transform into the shorter producer-to-menhaden-to-osprey route with two step blocks. The route changes while the osprey remains in place. Show the order only as the numbered step blocks; every organism keeps its own colour.
scenes.narration: On the longer path, the osprey is a third-order consumer. On a shorter path, it is second-order. The animal stays the same. Its order depends on the chosen path. Consumer order describes a position on one route.

scenes.tts: Dead matter and wastes carry stored energy from every level. Dashed routes lead downward to decomposers, including many bacteria and fungi. Their work returns matter, but energy keeps moving onward. The decomposer branch connects to every feeding level, not just the top.
scenes.visual: Small pieces from GREEN, BLUE, ORANGE, and PURPLE organisms drift downward. GREY dashed routes grow toward a large moving decomposer patch. GOLD specks travel with the material. A small GREY matter loop begins forming, while the GOLD energy route remains one-way.
scenes.narration: Dead matter and wastes carry stored energy from every level. Dashed routes lead downward to decomposers, including many bacteria and fungi. Their work returns matter, but energy keeps moving onward. The decomposer branch connects to every feeding level, not just the top.

scenes.tts: Now watch each feeding step. Much energy follows other routes, so the packet continuing upward becomes smaller. Energy has not disappeared; different paths now hold it or release heat. At each feeding step, less energy is available to the next level.
scenes.visual: Run several large GOLD packets into GREEN producers. At each feeding arrow, split off RED heat waves and GREY downward routes. Make the packet that continues to BLUE, ORANGE, and PURPLE visibly smaller. Show no percentage. On the guiding rule, hold the full moving web and show 'less available at each step'.
scenes.narration: Now watch each feeding step. Much energy follows other routes, so the packet continuing upward becomes smaller. Energy has not disappeared; different paths now hold it or release heat. At each feeding step, less energy is available to the next level.

scenes.tts: The osprey's energy began with sunlight captured by producers. A food web shows many connected routes. The shrinking packet explains why higher feeding levels have less energy to share. The web maps routes, while the packet maps what remains available.
scenes.visual: Trace one final GOLD packet from the sun through several branches. Pull back to show a large ORANGE school and one PURPLE osprey. Keep RED heat spreading and GREY decomposer routes moving. Fade all labels while the full Bay continues moving.
scenes.narration: The osprey's energy began with sunlight captured by producers. A food web shows many connected routes. The shrinking packet explains why higher feeding levels have less energy to share. The web maps routes, while the packet maps what remains available.

scenes.visual: Dim the Bay and show one line only: 'At each feeding step, less energy is available to the next level.'
